Subject: Clarify current SOC 2 package and bridge coverage

Hi Rishi,

We pulled the SOC 2 package from your compliance portal yesterday and noticed the PDF labelled "Redwood_SOC2_2023_TypeII.pdf" — our procurement/security team flagged it as out-of-date for our vendor acceptance window. Can you confirm which report is the canonical Type II (report ID if you have one) and whether you have a bridge or interim attestation that covers up through at least 2026-06-30?

Specifically our security reviewers asked for:
- Canonical report filename + report ID
- Auditor contact for verification
- Bridge letter or interim attestation dates to cover the gap (if any)
- Evidence index for encryption, key management, and retention policies (we require specific file names or links)

We also run SIG/CAIQ scans and may need the CAIQ export. If there is a preferred sharing method (DocSend / secure S3 link / NDA), please advise.

Thanks,
Jamie Liu
Director, Vendor Security
Acme Health

Hi Jamie,

Thanks for the note and for catching that. Apologies for the naming confusion — the file labelled "Redwood_SOC2_2023_TypeII.pdf" is an older artifact from our 2023 engagement (Report ID: RID-2023-v2). We are in the process of finalizing the reissued Type II for the period ending 2026-06-30; that reissued package will carry a new report ID.

Options we can provide immediately:
- Interim bridge letter signed by our auditor (PRISM) that explicitly covers 2024-07-01 through 2026-06-30. This is what most buyers accept when the final report is in production.
- A signed attestation from our Compliance team plus access to our evidence index (spreadsheet of evidence references).

I attached a short index (SOC2_package_index_v1.csv) showing how our packages are named so you can map older filenames to the upcoming package. If you’ll accept the bridge letter, I can coordinate PRISM to send a direct verification email to your auditor contact (audit@prism-audit.com) and deliver the bridge as a PDF and a follow-on evidence index (xlsx).

What would work for you here — bridge letter + evidence index, or an interim attestation? Also let me know if DocSend is acceptable for sharing the sensitive evidence files.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales (Security & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — bridge letter + evidence index is our preferred path. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Bridge wording: must explicitly state the coverage window (2024-07-01 through 2026-06-30) and reference the forthcoming final report ID if available.
2) Auditor verification: we will reach out to audit@prism-audit.com for independent confirmation; please have PRISM provide a contact name and phone.
3) Evidence requests (priority):
   - Encryption at rest architecture (diagram + KMS key rotation policy)
   - Data retention policy + S3 lifecycle rules for logs and backups
   - Access control evidence for production (IAM role list + sample access review)

DocSend is fine for sharing sensitive files; we can sign an NDA if required for any PII screenshots. Please include any DocSend links in your reply and the corresponding filename in the email body.

If you can send the bridge letter and a preliminary evidence index by EOD Aug 21 that would help us move forward with procurement.

Jamie
